items: The smallest useful piece of data is the **character**: any letter, number, or special symbol.
A **field** is a group of characters that has some meaning.
A **record** is a collection of fields containing data about an entity.

blocks.value:
character  →  field       →  record                        →  file
'A'           "Ana Reyes"    Ana Reyes,19,92.5                students.txt
When each record is accessed one after another in the order it was stored, the file is used as a **sequential access file**.
A record's fields can be organized into a single line or separated by a character. Values separated by commas are **comma-separated values**.

items: **A stream is a flow of data.** Data taken from a source (a file, the keyboard) into a program is an **input stream**. Data delivered from a program to a destination (a file, the screen) is an **output stream**.
**A buffer is a memory location into which you can write data and read it again later.**
**Flushing** clears any bytes sent to a buffer for output but not yet written out.

blocks.value: Buffering exists for speed: writing one character at a time to a disk is enormously slower than collecting a few thousand and writing them at once. The cost is that **data sitting in a buffer has not reached the file yet**, which is why closing a stream matters.
